content: Has anyone worked on representation theory of finite groups over C?
@Jalex Stark Not that I now of. At some point @Ben McDonnell worked on it a bit.
But that shouldn't stop you at all from attacking it.
Note that we would first need that basics which shouldn't be done for finite groups, but just in general.

Hi, I wanted to know the current status of Representation theory of finite groups. I see in the list of undergrad math that is not yet formalized.

Is there someone already working on it?

Abel Doñate Muñoz said:

What do you want to formalise to be exact? The list might not be updated often enough so there may be things in the list that was already in mathlib

In the page the section of Group Theory says that it is not yet formalized:

Representation theory of finite groups: representation of abelian groups, dual groups, Fourier transform for finite abelian groups, etc

I would like to know if some of them are formalized (mainly the three that I mention, not the etc. part)
I have the Fourier theory of finite abelian groups in YaelDillies/apap. I am currently working on generalising this to compact groups in YaelDillies/mean-fourier
